Example input: All_results_table.csv from HDXExaminer

Source: R/example_data.R
All_results_table.Rd

The package ships one example HDXExaminer "All results" export, used by the examples, tests and vignettes. It is a file, not an R object - get its path with system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR"). It holds two protein states ("Unbound", "bound"), four labeling times (3 s, 60 s, 1800 s, 72000 s) plus undeuterated (0s) and fully deuterated (FD) controls, and three replicates per state and time.

Format

A csv file with one row per peptide, charge state, protein state, labeling time and replicate:

Protein State

protein state name

Deut Time

labeling time, e.g. "3.00s"; "0s" undeuterated, "FD" fully deuterated

Experiment

replicate (experiment) name

Start

first residue number of the peptide

End

last residue number of the peptide

Sequence

amino acid sequence

Adduct

adduct ion

Charge

peptide charge state

Search RT

search retention time

Actual RT

actual retention time range

# Spectra

number of spectra

Search IMS

search ion-mobility value

IMS Range

ion-mobility range

Peak Width

peak width

m/z Shift

m/z shift

Max Inty

maximum intensity

Exp Cent

measured centroid (m/z)

Theor Cent

theoretical centroid (m/z)

Score

fit score

Cent Diff

centroid difference

# Deut

deuterium uptake (Da)

Deut %

percent deuteration

Mark

user mark

Confidence

HDXExaminer confidence level

Source

Cook M, Delbecq SP, Schweppe TP, Guttman M, Klevit RE, Brzovic PS. The ubiquitin ligase SspH1 from Salmonella uses a modular and dynamic E3 domain to catalyze substrate ubiquitylation. J Biol Chem. 2019;294(3):783-793. doi:10.1074/jbc.RA118.004247

Details

How to prepare this export from your own HDXExaminer project:

  1. Peptides tab > Pool > right-click a peptide - delete peptides with no usable data.

  2. Tools > Options > Display > Deuteration Table - display all columns (low-confidence results were not shown for this file).

  3. Tools > Export > All results table.
